name: Atom-cloud brain scanner
subtitle: a helmet that maps thought without surgery

effects.effect: atoms cooled almost to absolute zero behave as a single wave
electrodes on the motor cortex let a person's intent move a cursor or arm

effect: atoms cooled almost to absolute zero behave as a single wave
how: Decoding speech or intent from the brain today needs surgery, because the magnetic whisper a thought makes outside the skull is a billionth of the Earth's own field, and only a liquid-helium machine in a shielded room can hear it. A cloud of atoms chilled until they act as one wave tilts measurably in that whisper, and such a cell can sit against the scalp, so a helmet of them could map which patch of brain spoke, through the skull, for a person who can move.
obstacle: Each cell needs a vacuum and near-absolute-zero atoms while the Earth's field, a thousand million times stronger, is cancelled around a head that moves.
why: The only route to surgery-free, room-free brain reading sensitive enough to decode.
real: Rubidium BEC magnetometers with record energy resolution are promoted for future brain sensing but have never measured brain signals; all wearable-helmet MEG demonstrated to date (UCL/Nottingham, ~60 channels) uses room-temperature optically pumped magnetometers, a different mechanism.
